key_insight: A memory-to-delay reduction enables optimistic constrained online learning with guarantees that adapt to environmental change and prediction accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports stateful online decision-making and non-stochastic control under changing budget constraints while accommodating untrusted predictions.
method: Reduce memory effects to delayed feedback using state-dependent gradients.
Incorporate predictions into constrained online convex optimization without requiring functional separability.
Adapt dynamic-regret and cumulative-violation bounds to path length and prediction accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees, not empirical results: perfect predictions yield O(1) regret, with cumulative constraint violation O(√T) for unknown path length or O(log T) when path length is known or online observable.
watch_item: The stronger constraint-violation guarantee depends on path length being known or online observable, which may be difficult in practical deployments.
paper_title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence
